newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Details on bidders for Brazil's B Band service.
newsitem.headline: Details on bidders for Brazil's B Band service.

text.p: Fifteen consortia submitted bids to Brazil's Communications Ministry Monday to operate B Band cellular telephone concessions.

The ministry is expected to announce winners to the first two concessions, Sao Paulo city and the center west incorporated with parts of the Amazon, in late May with operations due to begin in December this year.
Below is a list of the companies involved in the bidding, as detailed by executives from each group.
Also included are the regional concessions they are bidding for. A table identifying the regions is below the list.
THE CONSORTIA

* Consorcio Avantel Comunicacoes Pessoais, made up of Brazilian contruction giants Odebrecht and Camargo Correa, Unibanco bank and AirTouch Communications of the United States. It has submitted bids for areas 1-6 and 9-10.
* Consorcio Brascom -- construction firm Andrade Gutierrez, industrial group Monteiro Aranha (both Brazil), Southwestern Bell (U.S.) and cellular operator Mannesmann Eurokom (Germany). Areas 1-6
* Consorcio Lightel -- private telecommunications operator Lightel, construction company Queiroz Galvao (both Brazil) and Korean Mobile Telecom. Areas 5, 6, 10.
* Consorcio Hutchison/Cowan -- telecommunications group Hutchison Whampoa (Hong Kong) and construction company Cowan Construtora (Brazil). Areas 4, 5.
* MCOM Wireless -- The investment wing of Banco Garantia, Garantia Participacoes (Brazil), Telmex (Mexico), Comcast (U.S.). Area 3.
* TT-2 Telecomunicacoes -- Bradesco bank and Globo Participacoes, the investment wing of the Globo media empire (both Brazil), AT&T and Stet. Areas 1, 2, 3.
* Consorcio Tess -- telecom operator Telia (Sweden), Airline Cellular (Brazil), and Primave, part of construction group CR Almeida (Brazil). Areas 1-6, 9-10
* Telet -- pension funds, publicly owned Banco do Brasil, Opportunity bank (Brazil), Bell Canada, (unit of BCE Citibank. Areas 1-6.
* BCP SA -- BellSouth Corp (U.S.), media group Estado de Sao Paulo, Banco Safra (Brazil), Splice. Areas 1-6.
* GFTT SA -- France Telecom, telecommunications venture Teldin (Brazil) and private equity funds of Banco Garantia. Areas 1, 3, 5, 10
* Consorcio Algar -- same as Consorcio Lightel. Area 3
* BSE SA -- same as BCP SA. Areas 9, 10.
* Americel SA -- same as Telet. Areas 7, 9, 10.
* Vicunha Telecomunicacoes Ltda -- industrial group Vicunha, Bradesco bank, Globo Participacoes (Brazil) and Stet (Italy). Areas 4, 5, 6, 9, 10.

* Consorcio Global Telecom -- paper producer Suzano, construction firm Inepar, (both Brazil), telecom operator DDI and trading company Nissho Iwai (both Japan) and Motorola Inc (U.S). Areas 2, 4, 5, 6.
AREAS
1. Sao Paulo city 2. The rest of Sao Paulo state
3. Rio de Janeiro and Espirito Santo states
4. Minas Gerais state
5. Parana and Santa Catarina states
6. Rio Grande do Sul state
7. Center western region, including capital Brasilia and Goais state, plus the Amazonian states of Acre, Rondonia, Tocantins.
8. The rest of the northern region (Para, Amazonas, Roraima and Amapa states) and Maranhao state
9. Bahia and Sergipe states
10. The rest of the northeast (Ceara, Rio Grande do Norte, Paraiba, Pernambuco, Alagoas, Piaui states).
NOTE: No bids were received for region No. 8.
(( -- William Schomberg, Brasilia newsroom 5561 2230358))
